providers.service_territory: Anchorage (North & South Districts), Girdwood, Whittier, Cooper Landing, Tyonek; largest electric cooperative in Alaska
providers.notes: Largest electric cooperative in Alaska; regulated by the Regulatory Commission of Alaska (RCA). Completed major rate case February 2025; new base rate filing August 2025 seeking 3% increase.

providers.service_territory: Fairbanks and surrounding interior Alaska communities; approximately 36,000 members across 6,440 square miles
providers.notes: Second-largest electric cooperative in Alaska. Has a Commercial Light Retrofit Rebate Program (documented by EPA). 2025 Rate Case filed with RCA; June 2025 saw 5% increase to Utility and Demand charges.

providers.service_territory: Mat-Su Valley (Palmer, Wasilla, Houston), parts of Anchorage outskirts; approximately 71,000 members
providers.notes: Alaska's second-largest member-owned electric cooperative by member count. Three-phase commercial accounts have access to demand charge and COPA surcharge rates. Rates reviewed quarterly.

providers.service_territory: Kenai Peninsula including Homer, Kenai, Soldotna, and surrounding communities
providers.notes: Offers heat pump rebate program for residential and commercial members. COPA (Cost of Power Adjustment) filed quarterly with RCA. Base rate increase of 4% proposed effective January 1, 2026.

Investor-owned utility serving Juneau. Primarily hydroelectric generation. Offers a special EV TOU rate (50% discount via separate meter at $0.05/kWh vs standard $0.10/kWh). No documented commercial energy efficiency rebate program found as of 2025.

providers.service_territory: 40 rural communities in Southeast Alaska, Interior, and Southcentral Alaska
providers.notes: Serves 40 rural/remote communities. Offers EV purchase rebate ($500) and EV charger rebate for local/tribal governments (up to $1,000). Limited commercial energy efficiency rebate documentation found; primarily residential and EV-focused programs.
Serves Kodiak Island. Offers EV charger rebate (up to $500 for residential). Primarily hydro and wind generation. Limited commercial rebate program documentation found; check directly with utility.

programs.program_notes_ai: Open to residential and commercial members. Covers air-source and ground-source heat pumps providing heating and/or cooling. Most beneficial to members without access to natural gas service. Pilot program subject to change.

programs.stacking_rules: Maximum of two incentive payments per location (per Chugach account number); one incentive per charger (one or two connectors)
programs.program_notes_ai: Open to Small General Service or Large General Service members. DC fast chargers may connect to existing LGS service or via new meter eligible for special EV Charging Tariff 87.1.1. Pre-approval recommended to confirm funding availability. Line extension credits may also be available.

programs.stacking_rules: Up to two rebates per billing account; one rebate per charger
programs.program_notes_ai: Incentives up to $1,000 per port for Level 2 chargers for commercial customers. Helps businesses, workplaces, fleet, and public charging installations. Pre-approval for funding availability recommended before construction.

Documented by EPA as a GVEA commercial lighting rebate program. Focused on commercial lighting retrofit projects. Specific rebate levels and current application form should be confirmed directly with GVEA. 2025 Rate Case in progress may affect program budget.

programs.stacking_rules: Members encouraged to also explore Alaska Heat Smart ACES Program for additional incentive stacking
programs.program_notes_ai: Covers air-source and ground-source heat pumps. Most beneficial to members using heating oil or propane, or with outdated electric heating. Members may stack with Alaska Heat Smart Accelerating Clean Energy Savings (ACES) Program. HEA notes homes on natural gas may not see significant savings.

MEA is Alaska's second-largest cooperative by member count (~71,000 members in Mat-Su). Specific commercial rebate details and current application forms should be confirmed directly with MEA. Rates reviewed quarterly with COPA surcharge adjustments.

rate_schedules.description: Non-residential consumers whose demand does not exceed 20 kW at any time during the billing month. South District covers South Anchorage, Girdwood, Whittier, Seward Highway corridor.
rate_schedules.notes: Rates effective as of February 2025 (post rate case). July 2026 rates now in effect per Chugach website. Specific kWh and customer charge figures require direct tariff PDF review. No demand charge applies below 20 kW threshold.

rate_schedules.description: Non-residential consumers whose demand exceeds 20 kW. Demand ratchet eliminated for large commercial customers effective February 2025 — customers now pay actual demand in current billing period only.
rate_schedules.notes: RCA approved elimination of 11-month demand ratchet for large commercial in 2025 rate case. August 2025 base rate filing seeks additional ~3% increase. Specific tariff figures require direct PDF review.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Small General Service – North District (former ML&P)
rate_schedules.description: Downtown Anchorage and East Anchorage (formerly served by Municipal Light & Power). Rates in effect as of October 1, 2025.
rate_schedules.notes: North District (former ML&P territory) was integrated into Chugach system after 2020 acquisition. Rates set separately from South District but subject to same RCA oversight. 2% undergrounding surcharge applies to MOA customers.

rate_schedules.schedule_name: Large General Service – North District (former ML&P)
rate_schedules.description: Large commercial/industrial customers (demand >20 kW) in former ML&P service territory (Downtown and East Anchorage).
rate_schedules.notes: Tariff No. 8 (RCA). Specific rates require direct tariff PDF download. North District commercial rates may differ from South District.

rate_schedules.description: Special DC fast charging tariff rate available to Large General Service members installing DC fast chargers via a new meter. Referenced as Tariff 87.1.1.
rate_schedules.notes: Available as an alternative to standard LGS rate for dedicated EV charging meters. Specific rate details require RCA tariff filing review.

rate_schedules.description: Special rate schedule for ship interconnections on the Chugach system. Designed to incentivize shore power use instead of burning vessel fuel while in port, supporting lower carbon emissions.
rate_schedules.notes: New schedule approved in 2025 rate case. Specific rates require RCA tariff filing review.

rate_schedules.description: GVEA offers 5 rate classifications depending on service type. Rates vary for residential vs. business. Effective Rate = Fuel & Purchased Power Charge + Utility Charge + Regulatory Charge + ERO Charge. F&PP rate dropped from 12.899¢ to 11.553¢/kWh effective September 1, 2025.
rate_schedules.notes: Utility and Demand charges increased 5% effective June 1, 2025. 2025 Rate Case filed with RCA. Effective composite rate is a sum of multiple components.

rate_schedules.description: Large commercial/industrial service with demand charges. Demand charges increased 5% effective June 1, 2025 per GVEA SRF filing.
rate_schedules.notes: Specific demand charge $/kW and energy charge $/kWh require direct tariff review. F&PP pass-through has no markup — actual cost of generation/purchased power only.

rate_schedules.description: Three-phase commercial accounts. Base rate: $30/month facilities charge + $9.29/kW demand charge + $0.10302/kWh energy charge, plus COPA surcharge of $0.07879/kWh (Q2 2026). All-in effective rate approximately $0.18/kWh combined.
rate_schedules.notes: COPA surcharge adjusted quarterly. Q3 2025 saw 3% base rate increase + 12.2% COPA increase. Q2 2026 COPA rose ~3.2%. Large loads may qualify for negotiated Large Power Contract Rate Service.

rate_schedules.description: Negotiated rate for very large commercial/industrial loads. Terms set by contract with MEA.
rate_schedules.notes: Available for large loads only. Specific rates negotiated individually; contact MEA directly.

rate_schedules.description: All general services using more than 20 kW of monthly demand during 3 consecutive months, but less than 1,000 kW of monthly demand. HEA offers four rate classifications total.
rate_schedules.notes: HEA's COPA filed quarterly and reviewed by RCA. COPA expected to range $0.091–$0.093/kWh effective January 2026 (a ~13–15% decrease). ERO Surcharge of $0.000720/kWh also applies as of January 2026. Rate schedule effective April 1, 2026 per HEA website.

rate_schedules.description: Small non-residential commercial service (under 20 kW demand). One of four HEA rate classifications.
rate_schedules.notes: Regulated by RCA. COPA and ERO surcharges also apply. Specific kWh rates require HEA tariff schedule PDF review.

forms.form_notes: Application details available on Chugach's Beneficial Electrification page. Specific PDF form link should be confirmed directly at the program URL.
Members must complete application and provide proof of purchase and installation to receive bill credit. Pre-approval application also available and recommended prior to construction.

forms.form_name: Commercial Level 2 EV Charging Incentive Application
forms.form_notes: Application and proof of purchase/installation required. Pre-approval for funding availability recommended. Up to two applications per billing account allowed.
Application form should be obtained directly from GVEA. EPA documentation confirms program existence; current form and specific rebate amounts should be verified with GVEA directly.
Application and program details available on HEA's energy efficiency page. Members encouraged to also apply to Alaska Heat Smart ACES program for additional incentives.
Specific application form URL should be confirmed directly with MEA. Contact MEA at 907-745-3231 for current program documents.
